q-214694.name: Question 1
q-214694.worked_solution:
We isolate $x$ by applying the addition principle, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & \le 3x+5\le 8 \\ -1-5 & \le 3x+5-5\le 8-5 \\ -6 & \le 3x\le 3 \\ \frac{-6}{3} & \le \frac{3x}{3}\le \frac{3}{3} \\ -2 & \le x\le 1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $-2\le x\le 1.$

q-214755.name: Question 2
q-214755.worked_solution:
We isolate $x$ by applying the addition and multiplication principles, as usual.

First, we multiply by $3$ to eliminate the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & <\frac{x+5}{3}\le 2 \\ 3\cdot 1 & <3\cdot \frac{x+5}{3}\le 3\cdot 2 \\ 3 & <x+5\le 6\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we continue isolating $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & <x+5\le 6 \\ 3-5 & <x+5-5\le 6-5 \\ -2 & <x\le 1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $-2<x\le 1.$

q-214767.name: Question 3
q-214767.worked_solution:
We isolate $x$ by applying the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & \le -4x+6<10 \\ 2-6 & \le -4x+6-6<10-6 \\ -4 & \le -4x<4\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide by $-4.$ Note that since we are dividing by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality signs.

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & \le -4x<4 \\ \frac{-4}{-4} & \ge \frac{-4x}{-4}>\frac{4}{-4} \\ 1 & \ge x>-1\end{aligned}
$$

The solution can be written as $1\ge x>-1$, but this is somewhat difficult to read because the larger number is on the left rather than the right. So, we will rewrite the solution by reversing the order of the numbers: 

Therefore, the solution is $-1<x\le 1.$

q-3070.name: Question 4
q-3070.worked_solution:
We isolate $x$ by applying the addition and multiplication principles, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}-10 & <\frac{6-2x}{3}<0 \\ 3\cdot (-10) & <3\cdot (\frac{6-2x}{3})<3\cdot 0 \\ -30 & <6-2x<0 \\ -30-6 & <6-2x-6<0-6 \\ -36 & <-2x<-6\end{aligned}
$$

At this point, we need to divide by $-2.$ However, because we are dividing by a negative, we also need to flip the inequality signs.

$$
\begin{aligned}-36 & <-2x<-6 \\ \frac{-36}{-2} & >\frac{-2x}{-2}>\frac{-6}{-2} \\ 18 & >x>3\end{aligned}
$$

The solution can be written as $18>x>3,$ but this is somewhat difficult to read because the larger number is on the left rather than the right. So, we will rewrite the solution by reversing the order of the numbers:

$$
3<x<18
$$

At this point, we need to divide by −2. However, because we are dividing by a negative, we also need to flip the inequality signs.

−36<−2x<−6−36−2>−2x−2>−6−218>x>3

q-44762.name: Question 5
q-44762.problem: Which of the following number lines gives the solution to $-13\le -5x+2\le -8?$
q-44762.worked_solution:
We isolate $x$  by applying the addition and multiplication principles, as usual.

First, we apply the addition principle:

$$
\begin{aligned}-13 & \le -5x+2\le -8 \\ -13-2 & \le -5x+2-2\le -8-2 \\ -15 & \le -5x\le -10\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide by $-5.$ Note that since we are dividing by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality signs. 

$$
\begin{aligned}-15 & \le -5x\le -10 \\ \frac{-15}{-5} & \ge \frac{-5x}{-5}\ge \frac{-10}{-5} \\ 3 & \ge x\ge 2\end{aligned}
$$

The solution can be written as $3\ge x\ge 2$, but this is somewhat difficult to read because the larger number is on the left rather than the right. So, we will rewrite the solution by reversing the order of the numbers: 

$$
2\le x\le 3.
$$

We can represent this solution using a number line, as follows.

q-102104.name: Question 6
q-102104.problem: Which of the following number lines gives the solution to $-2<\frac{1-3x}{4}\le 1?$
q-102104.worked_solution:
We isolate $x$ by applying the addition and multiplication principles, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2 & <\frac{1-3x}{4}\le 1 \\ -2\cdot 4 & <\frac{1-3x}{4}\cdot 4\le 1\cdot 4 \\ -8 & <1-3x\le 4 \\ -8-1 & <1-3x-1\le 4-1 \\ -9 & <-3x\le 3\end{aligned}
$$

At this point, we need to divide by $-3.$ However, because we are dividing by a negative, we also need to flip the inequality signs.

$$
\begin{aligned}-9 & <-3x\le 3 \\ \frac{-9}{-3} & >\frac{-3x}{-3}\ge \frac{3}{-3} \\ 3 & >x\ge -1\end{aligned}
$$

The solution can be written as $3>x\ge -1$,  but this is somewhat difficult to read because the larger number is on the left rather than the right. So, we will rewrite the solution by reversing the order of the numbers: 

$$
-1\le x<3
$$

We can represent this solution using a number line, as follows.
